entries.description: OurRelationship program produces reliable improvements in relationship functioning relative to a 6-month waitlist control group for low-income couples seeking help
entries.citation_sentence: In the current study, we report on a subset of these couples- those whose treatment assignments replicated those in Doss et al. (2020).

entries.original_title: Online programs improve relationship functioning for distressed low-income couples: Results from a nationwide randomized controlled trial
entries.original_authors: Doss, B. D.; Knopp, K.; Roddy, M. K.; Rothman, K.; Hatch, S. G.; Rhoades, G. K.
entries.original_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
entries.description: OurRelationship program produces greater reductions in communication conflict than ePREP program for low-income couples seeking help
entries.citation_sentence: In the current study, we report on a subset of these couples- those whose treatment assignments replicated those in Doss et al. (2020).
entries.notes: Frequentist analysis shows no statistically reliable difference between programs on communication conflict, but Bayesian analysis provides evidence supporting the original differential effect. The 95% credible interval for the differential effect barely includes zero [-.348, .002].
